stem: Petechiae and purpura are described as non-blanching spots. What does 'non-blanching' mean in a clinical context?

options.text: The spots disappear when you press on them.
The spots do not disappear or turn white when pressure is applied.
The spots are itchy and raised above the skin surface.
The spots only appear on mucous membranes.

explanation: Non-blanching means the blood has leaked out of the vessels into the skin, so pressing on it does not move the blood or change the color.
rationale: Consider what happens to a bruise when you push on it compared to a standard red rash.

optionExplanations.A: That describes a blanching rash, which is usually inflammatory or infectious but not hemorrhagic.
optionExplanations.B: Non-blanching means the blood has leaked out of the vessels into the skin, so pressing on it does not move the blood or change the color.
optionExplanations.C: Itchiness and elevation are characteristics of hives or other dermatological conditions, not necessarily petechiae.
optionExplanations.D: While they can appear on mucous membranes (wet purpura), they frequently appear on the skin.
